name: Evolution — Living Population
description: Fig 11b — evolution by natural selection as a genuine place-graph rewrite you can play forward. A `population` (tree[node]) of identically-schema'd `cell` nodes — each with a heritable scalar `trait` and a derived `division_rate` — evolves under an `environment` whose `selection_optimum` gently DRIFTS over time (starting above zero). Each generation the optimum shifts, each cell's division rate is re-scored by trait↔optimum fit, and cells undergo BINARY FISSION: a dividing cell is REPLACED by two daughters, each inheriting its trait ± Gaussian mutation (the founder does not persist once it divides). The population grows to carrying capacity; beyond it the least-fit cells (furthest from the optimum) die. Over many generations the whole trait cloud tracks the drifting optimum — selection + mutation + division. Steppable topology for the loom run/animate feature.

optimum0.description: Starting favored trait value (the optimum at t=0).

drift.description: Shift of the selection optimum per generation (gentle moving target).

sel_strength.description: Selection sharpness — the Gaussian fitness width (fitness = e^{-s·Δ²}).

mut_sigma.description: Standard deviation of the heritable mutation step passed to each daughter.

div_rate.description: Per-generation division probability for a perfectly-fit cell.
